setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: "I know Kim called you yesterday to reschedule."

prospect.name: Mike Terpin
prospect.aka: Samsung SM-F766U (joined from a phone; device model is the only speaker label in the transcript)
prospect.training_background: Former Division I athlete with an explicit working knowledge of strength training and bodybuilding programming — "I understand, like, strength training, bodybuilding, the difference between, you know, the different types... a rep range of an 8 to 10 if you're trying to build some muscle is a solid way to go with a progressive overload." Already training with kettlebells for some time.

signals: Former Division I athlete, already training consistently, explicitly not a rescue case — rep: "it's not like you're coming here eating donuts never worked out before, right?" — prospect: "No, definitely not."
Buying direction and programming rather than transformation: "a little bit more like focused direction would be"
Confidence is low by necessity — the recording ends at 00:04:14 before baseline, goals, occupation or finances were reached, so this assignment rests on four minutes of material

goals.text: Get kettlebell programming that is structured toward an actual outcome rather than just producing fatigue
Train in flows — stringing movements together — rather than conventional straight-set bodybuilding schemes

pains.text: Effort is not converting into results — "it's just a lot of like work but not necessarily productivity that I end up doing"
His sessions vary session to session with no through-line — "it kind of varies, which is part of the problem"
Conventional progressive-overload rep schemes work but bore him — "it gets boring, you know, I'm not really trying to be a bodybuilder"
Cannot assemble the free workouts he likes into a coherent plan — "how would I string these together to, like, actually accomplish something, versus, like, just get really tired?"

evidence: The recording ends mid-conversation at 00:04:14 on a connection failure: "Oh, you cut out now too? You there?"
The rep had flagged connectivity trouble from the opening — "my Wi-Fi has been messing up all day"
The call had only reached the opening of discovery; no offer, no price, no objection and no decision of any kind occurred on the recorded portion
Whether the call resumed after the dropout, was rescheduled, or was abandoned is not recoverable from this file — no continuation file appears in the batch

notable.note: Not a junk file by the size rule (4,005 bytes, above the 2,000-byte threshold) but functionally a fragment: four minutes of a call that dropped on a connection failure the rep had already reported at the top. Kept in the corpus as undetermined; it must not be counted in any close-rate denominator without a note, and it is the second file in this batch where the technical record rather than the sales process decides the outcome. The prospect appears only as a device model, Samsung SM-F766U.

quality.notes: Truncated and swapped. The rep's own frame-setting and open question at 00:00:31-00:00:42 are split across both labels, and at 00:00:49 the prospect label carries the rep's question echoed back verbatim ("What was it that you were hoping we could potentially help you out with?"), which is an artefact rather than a real turn. The prospect is identified only by a phone device label throughout; the name comes from the title.
